"Basically, want them to know and feel how unhinged and how heinous I can be. I think the sense of danger has been lost in wrestling a lot. A lot of it's good in entertainment and stuff like that, but there hasn't been a big sense of fear and danger that feels absolutely real," he explained to OutKick Dropkick.

"When I walk out the curtain, I want them to feel that oh s--- moment that this is about to get serious and ‘I need to be on my guard, my toes to pay attention about what's about to happen because who knows, I could be next.’ That's the feeling I want to introduce to people and what's coming up. For me, I feel that elevated danger is going to start to rise more and more."

MLW announced earlier this month it would show its weekly series, "Fusion," on Tubi.

"It’s incredible to be honest," Savage said. "Man, to already be part of the MLW roster and be part of Contra is already amazing, and then getting a Tubi deal to air free on Thursdays is absolutely insane. They're moving so fast at connecting all these pieces, it's actually incredible.

"They're one of the fastest growing wrestling companies out there. And being on Tubi, right, and just say, ‘Hey, go watch me on Tubi,’ and people being able to pull up the app, pull it up on their TVs, pull it up on their phones, watch it wherever they are is absolutely incredible. So, it's an insane feeling to be a part of. So happy about that."

item.title: CMLL talents look to increase popularity among American pro wrestling fans with latest opportunity
item.description: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre's AEW partnership now lets U.S. fans stream CMLL shows on MyAEW, solving the long-standing access problem for Lucha Libre.
item.content:encoded:
Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) is one of the most historic pro wrestling promotions on the planet. The company was founded in 1933 and continues to honor Lucha Libre style wrestling to this day.

As pro wrestling’s popularity has increased dramatically over the years, CMLL has had the need to get more eyeballs on its product. Among the steps the company has taken, CMLL partnered with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) to feature its superstars on its programming. The partnership has allowed CMLL legends like Místico to appear at AEW and Ring of Honor shows while still being the generational figure that he is in Mexico. The same has held true for a lot of CMLL talent.

The next step was to find a footing in the United States. With immense potential, CMLL held its first solo event in Las Vegas as part of Slam Fest during WrestleMania weekend. The action-packed event saw the likes of Blue Panther, Ultimo Guerrero, Persephone, Tessa Blanchard, Místico, Hechicero, Templario, Angel de Oro and others showcase their talent.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Passionate pro wrestling fans could easily get hooked on the athleticism and storytelling that CMLL brings in the ring. But what about watching it at home? Where can the average pro wrestling fan watch incredible Lucha Libre? MyAEW was launched with that concept in mind – giving fans access to events they normally wouldn’t be able to find elsewhere.

CMLL’s New Japan Pro-Wrestling Fantastica Mania Mexico 2026 was added to the event schedule. Several more shows were added to the docket after that, including the company’s anniversary event which was held back on Sept. 18.

"This is a huge deal," CMLL Mexican national champion Thunder Rosa told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview. "A lot of people have been asking for a long time, how can they watch CMLL, right? And I think right now CMLL is at a point in where it's known globally. I mean, it's known globally like people every time that they come to Mexico City, they come to Arena, México to experience what Lucha Libre is. But it's always been like this dark area and like, Where can I watch this? And they were like you can go on YouTube. CMLL has had a subscription based activity with YouTube and where you can watch all the CMLL stuff in there but now they partner with AEW with this big partnership that we have had on this almost for two years and now people in America, if you have access to MyAEW.com you can watch the shows.

"It excites me because as someone who works in both companies, now I can tell people, if you have MyAEW.com now you can watch CMLL and I hope that a lot of the other programming from CMLL is there too because there's been fantastic matches in the last I want to say last year. CMLL just in general has the best wrestling in the world. Just like AEW where the best wrestle, CMLL is we're the best wrestle."

Miguel Castro wears many hats for CMLL. But most who tune into the English-speaking commentary will hear his voice on the broadcast.

Castro said that while AEW has given CMLL as platform to showcase the best it has to offer, trying to carve out an audience and build a brand in the United States is a challenge in and of itself.

"Mostly brand recognition," Castro told OutKick Dropkick when asked what were some of the obstacles in the way of growth in the U.S. "I believe that our talents’ work speaks for itself. Anyone that enjoys wrestling, even if you like it by 5% compared to a fan, you will enjoy a CMLL show. It's not all about the drama and the storytelling, and that, I think that's what has made such a good connection with AEW and with New Japan Pro-Wrestling, we're heavily focused on the sports. So, even if you've never seen wrestling and you go to a CMLL show, you will enjoy it. It's fun. It'll make you gasp, it will make you scream, you'll have fun, and then you're gonna want to know more."

Castro added that CMLL has very little, if at all, advertising budget and still sells out Arena México for its shows. He credited AEW for giving CMLL a showcase for its talent, brand and helping create stars in the U.S. If Místico is on the card in an AEW or Ring of Honor show, fans will sing his entrance music "Me Muero." Persephone has become a rising star in AEW as she won the TBS Championship at All In.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Ultimately, Castro said the biggest obstacle is doing something CMLL has never done before and if fans can get eyes on the product, they will return.

But what would success look like to Castro come September 2027?

"I would love to increase the pay-per-view numbers 10 times on MyAEW and I know that's going to happen as they also grow their base in the platform," he said. "My main focus right now would be to have a media deal in the States. And ideally not in Univision or Telemundo. Like I don't want it to be part of a TV station just because it's Mexican. That, for me, would be huge. It's very probable that we're not going to get there so soon, especially because we haven't even started trying to have those conversations with people.

"But we just started three months ago with Fox Sports in Mexico and I can tell you that we're getting about a million pairs of eyeballs every month. That's been huge because we had our YouTube, like that's the thing. If we could do that, I would think I would consider that very successful. I would also love that during next year."

Fantastica Mania is next on the CMLL docket. It will partner with RevPro on the showcase, which takes placet Oct. 17 and 18. Both shows are available for purchase for $14.99.

item.title: Canadian broadcaster reportedly pulled after recording anti-Israel protest outside service
item.description: Newsreader Neil Herland's viral video of an anti-Israel protest outside a Toronto synagogue service on Yom Kippur reportedly led CBC to pull him off-air.
item.content:encoded:
Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) newsreader Neil Herland was reportedly pulled off the air and faced an internal investigation after posting a video of an anti-Israel protest outside a synagogue service last week.

Herland documented himself attempting to enter a service held by The Song Shul at the Meridian Arts Centre that was protested by about two dozen demonstrators holding signs and noisemakers while chanting, "Free, Free Palestine."

"I'm a journalist. And I happen to be Jewish. On Yom Kippur I went to a synagogue service in Toronto and was met by protesters trying to taunt and intimidate me from entering the building," Herland wrote on X.

ANTI-ISRAEL AGITATORS CLASH WITH NYPD OFFICERS NEAR SYNAGOGUE

In the video, a man shouted "Zionist alert" as Herland approached the building, and Herland was accosted by a man shouting, "You're going to hell" for attending the service, which featured Israeli diplomat and former Benjamin Netanyahu advisor Mark Regev as a speaker.

In follow-up comments, Herland emphasized his growing concerns that Canada itself may no longer be safe for Jewish people.

"My late father was an Austrian Jew who survived the Holocaust in Romania. And came to Canada as a refugee. This year I got an Austrian passport, in case Canada becomes unsafe for me as a Jew. I fear that moment is approaching, here in Canada and elsewhere," Herland wrote.

"Jewish Canadians are living in a parallel world," he added. "Where police stand guard with guns outside synagogues. And Jewish schools, religious sites and businesses are targeted with bullets. And most Canadians have no awareness or understanding."

CANADA'S CARNEY PLEDGES ACTION ON ANTISEMITISM AMID BACKLASH OVER NEW ANTI-HATE COUNCIL MEMBERS

The video has since received 3.8 million views.

After Herland posted his comments, The Toronto Sun reported Thursday that the veteran journalist was pulled from his on-air job and informed that he would be investigated based on complaints made to the company. Herland himself has not posted anything from his X account since Friday.

Though it is unclear what complaints could have led to this decision, the organization Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East (CJPME) encouraged followers on X to send in complaints, claiming that Herland was purposefully misleading people about the situation.

"On September 21, @CBC National Radio News Reader @NEWSneil Neil Herland posted on X that was 'met by [pro-Palestine] protesters trying to taunt and intimidate [him] from entering [a synagogue service in Toronto].' He shared an accompanying video of Palestine solidarity protesters."

"However, Herland was on his way to the Meridian Arts Centre, not a synogogue, to see Mark Regev. Regev was not merely a teacher and former Israeli ambassador, but served in multiple high-ranking positions in the Israeli government, including as the Prime Minister’s Senior Advisor for Foreign Affairs and International Communications and the International Spokesperson for the Prime Minister’s Office," the CJPME's post read.

CBC TELLS JOURNALISTS NOT TO CALL 9/11 ‘TERRORIST ATTACKS’ IN INTERNAL GUIDANCE

The post continued, "The reality is that Herland was telling a demonstrable lie to defame pro-Palestine activists. Join us in writing to the Values and Ethics Commissioner for CBC/Radio-Canada, Sherry Perreault, to express serious concerns about apparent ethics violations by Neil Herland."

When reached for comment, CBC spokesperson Chuck Thompson told Fox News Digital that CBC would not comment on the matter but claimed that reporting has been filled with "errors and mischaracterizations."

"Fully respecting the privacy rights of our employees, we don’t comment on internal matters. That said, we are aware of reporting on this matter which has errors and mischaracterizations but we can't get into the specifics given the confidentiality of the situation," Thompson said.

item.title: NCAA responds after Riley Gaines' lawsuit is dismissed, affirms compliance with Trump's executive order
item.description: Riley Gaines and fellow athletes plan to appeal after a federal judge dismissed their Title IX lawsuit, ruling the NCAA isn't a federal funding recipient.
item.content:encoded:
The NCAA defended its record on women’s sports after a federal judge dismissed Riley Gaines’ Title IX lawsuit against the organization, emphasizing its current compliance with President Donald Trump’s executive order without directly addressing the allegations underlying the case.

"The NCAA is proud to continually invest in and expand women’s sports and the NCAA is in full compliance with the Trump administration’s executive order on women’s sports," the organization said in a statement.

The Independent Council on Women's Sports (ICONS) responded to the NCAA statement in a social media post later on Tuesday.

"No promises to women. No assurances. No accountability. The weakest possible response: empty words on a page," the organization wrote.

The response came one day after U.S. District Judge Tiffany R. Johnson granted summary judgment to the NCAA on the lawsuit’s remaining Title IX claims and directed the clerk to close the case.

SUPREME COURT MAKES RULING ON TRANS ATHLETES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS

Johnson did not determine whether the NCAA’s former transgender-athlete policies discriminated against female athletes. Instead, the Biden-appointed judge concluded that the evidence did not establish the NCAA as a recipient of federal financial assistance, a requirement for liability under Title IX.

Gaines and more than a dozen other current and former female college athletes sued the NCAA in March 2024. They alleged the organization violated their Title IX rights through policies that allowed biological males to compete in women’s events and enter women’s locker rooms.

The case focused heavily on the 2022 NCAA Division I Women’s Swimming and Diving Championships, where former University of Pennsylvania swimmer Lia Thomas won the 500-yard freestyle and shared a locker room with female competitors. Gaines, then representing Kentucky, tied Thomas for fifth place in the 200-yard freestyle.

Gaines and the Independent Council on Women’s Sports, which funded the lawsuit, announced Monday that the plaintiffs intend to appeal the ruling to the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals.

"This momentary setback will not deter me or other women athletes in the least," Gaines said. "Rest assured, we will be appealing this decision."

The NCAA’s statement did not address the planned appeal, the plaintiffs’ criticism of its previous policy or whether the organization maintains that it is categorically beyond Title IX’s reach.

FEDERAL JUDGE DISMISSES DOJ LAWSUIT CHALLENGING CALIFORNIA POLICY ALLOWING BIOLOGICAL MALES IN GIRLS’ SPORTS

The ruling centered on the NCAA’s concussion-research collaboration with the Department of Defense. The plaintiffs argued that the arrangement made the organization an indirect recipient of federal funding.

Johnson found that the NCAA and the Defense Department maintained separate funding streams, with both contributing money to Indiana University for research conducted through the Concussion Assessment, Research and Education Consortium.

"Here, there is no evidence that the NCAA ever received, or could have received, federal funds," Johnson wrote. "Thus, Plaintiffs’ Title IX claims cannot proceed."

The policy challenged by Gaines and the other athletes is no longer in effect. Trump signed his "Keeping Men Out of Women’s Sports" executive order on Feb. 5, 2025, directing federal agencies to enforce Title IX based on biological sex.

The NCAA changed its participation policy the following day, limiting competition on women’s teams to athletes assigned female at birth. The current rules contain no waiver allowing athletes assigned male at birth to compete on women’s teams, although they may practice with those teams and receive benefits such as medical care while practicing. See ncaa.org.

ICONS co-founders Kim Jones and Marshi Smith have argued that the NCAA’s successful position that it was not covered by Title IX demonstrates that Congress should not provide the organization with additional authority through the Protect College Sports Act.

Smith said the NCAA "cannot be trusted to regulate anyone’s sports — men’s or women’s" and urged members of Congress to oppose the legislation after it passed the Senate on Monday.

The case’s appeal could now ask the 11th Circuit to decide whether the NCAA’s collaboration with the Defense Department, or its relationship with federally funded entities involved in the research, is sufficient to bring the organization within Title IX’s reach.

item.title: Wyoming man kicks mountain lion in the face to save his dog, then fights it off bare-handed
item.description: Adam Borkhus kicked a mountain lion in the face to save his dog Diesel near Cody, Wyoming, but the predator then pounced and knocked him down.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this month, a Wyoming man found himself in a situation no dog owner ever wants to imagine.

His Labrador was being attacked by a mountain lion.

So he did the only thing he could think to do. He kicked the big cat in the face.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Adam Borkhus, a 33-year-old amateur wildlife photographer, was out looking for elk near Cody, Wyo., on Sept. 19 when he stopped along a remote road to change camera lenses and let his 2-year-old Lab, Diesel, out of the vehicle.

Seconds later, he heard his dog yelp.

Borkhus ran into the brush and found a mountain lion on top of Diesel. He had both a firearm and bear spray with him, but with his dog tangled up with the cat, he didn't want to risk hitting Diesel with either.

So Borkhus went with Plan C: his foot.

A swift kick square in the mountain lion’s face successfully got the cat off Diesel. Unfortunately, it also got the cat's attention.

"The lion spun around and looked at me," Borkhus told Outside. "Then it pounced and hit me in the chest."

Borkhus — who stands 6-foot-3 and weighs roughly 300 pounds — was knocked onto his back by the approximately 70-pound cat. He said he tried to keep its teeth away from his face and neck while punching it with his free hand before eventually grabbing its ear and wrenching it hard enough that the lion took off.

The whole thing lasted somewhere around 20 to 30 seconds.

Borkhus escaped with scratches to his hands, arm and face. Diesel somehow came out of the ordeal without any injuries. And, while his owner was busy throwing hands with a mountain lion, he retreated to the vehicle.

BIG SKY, MONTANA WILDLIFE ENCOUNTER CAUGHT ON VIDEO AS MOOSE CHARGES TOWARD WOMAN AND HER DOGS

He was waiting for Borkhus at the tailgate.

Not much of a protective instinct there, but we’re sure Diesel is still a good boy anyway.

Kicking a mountain lion in the face worked out remarkably well for Borkhus. But it probably shouldn't be your first line of defense.

Wyoming Game and Fish says conflicts between humans and mountain lions are rare, but there are several things people should know when recreating in lion country.

For starters, don't approach one — which should be obvious. Give the animal room to escape and remain calm if you encounter one. The department recommends speaking calmly and firmly rather than running away. Traveling in groups can also reduce the chances of surprising a mountain lion in the first place.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

And if things go sideways? Fight back.

That's the official advice from Wyoming Game and Fish: "If a mountain lion attacks you, fight back and defend yourself."

Outside also spoke with Mountain Lion Foundation researcher Joshua Lisbon, who recommended keeping dogs leashed or under strong voice control while in the wilderness. If a lion does grab your dog, Lisbon recommends using bear spray rather than physically jumping into the fight — even if your dog gets sprayed in the process.

Obviously, that's much easier advice to process while sitting safely at home than when your best friend is underneath a mountain lion.

But thank goodness for Borkhus and Diesel, it worked out this time.

item.title: Supreme Court takes up fight over Trump’s third-country illegal alien deportation policy
item.description: The Supreme Court cleared Trump's third-country deportation policy to proceed while justices prepare to hear the full legal challenge in December.
item.content:encoded:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday handed the Trump administration an interim victory in its ongoing immigration crackdown, clearing the way for officials to continue deporting illegal aliens to third countries while the justices consider a legal challenge to the policy.

The justices granted the administration's request to stay a February ruling from a federal district court in Massachusetts that imposed additional procedural requirements before illegal immigrants could be removed to countries other than their own.

The high court also agreed to hear the administration's challenge, treating its emergency application as a petition for review and ordering the parties to prepare for arguments during the court's December session.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT DEALS BLOW TO TRUMP DEPORTATION AGENDA

Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson said they would have denied the administration's request for a stay.

The decision gives the administration the immediate relief it sought as it presses ahead with third-country removals, even as the Supreme Court has yet to decide whether the policy remains.

The dispute centers on the Trump administration's efforts to remove illegal aliens to third countries. Lower courts have not categorically prohibited those removals but have required procedures intended to give aliens an opportunity to raise claims that they could face persecution or torture in the destination country.

The Trump administration returned to the Supreme Court last week, arguing that those requirements were interfering with its ability to carry out removals and disrupting sensitive diplomatic negotiations with countries willing to accept deportees.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

"The order below also undermines our standing abroad," the administration argued in its filing, according to the ruling. "Finding third countries willing and able to accept aliens is a delicate diplomatic endeavor."

The government also argued that judicial intervention in those arrangements could cause "significant and irreparable harm to U.S. foreign policy."

Attorneys challenging their policy pushed back, arguing that the lower court's ruling did not prevent the administration from conducting third-country removals but instead required the government to provide notice and an opportunity for illegal aliens to raise protection claims before they were sent abroad.

"The judgment does not require release from detention, prohibit third-country removals, or undo existing arrangements," the challengers argued in their response.

DHS' TOP LAWYER THREATENS PENALTIES FOR ATTORNEYS CLOGGING ASYLUM SYSTEM

They alleged that illegal aliens removed without meaningful notice or an opportunity to raise country-specific protection claims had faced "prolonged and arbitrary detention, beatings and sexual assault, disappearance, and chain refoulement."

Tuesday's order puts the February district court judgment on hold while the Supreme Court considers the case. The stay will remain in effect until the high court sends down its judgment.

The decision gives the administration the immediate relief it sought as it presses ahead with third-country removals, even as the Supreme Court has yet to decide.

"For the third time in 18 months, the Supreme Court has been called upon to stay the same local district judge’s campaign to halt the Trump Administration from removing illegal aliens including many of the worst-of-the-worst criminals to countries willing to receive them," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital.

"The President will stop at nothing in his effort to make America safe again," Bis added. "Today’s ruling from the Supreme Court yet again affirms the lawfulness of the President’s homeland security agenda."

The court directed its clerk to establish a briefing schedule allowing the case to be argued during its December 2026 argument session.

item.title: Aaron Judge's calf strain could cascade into hamstring or Achilles injuries if rushed back, surgeon warns
item.description: Aaron Judge's soleus strain could lead to an Achilles rupture if he returned too soon, a surgeon warns, explaining the risks behind the New York Yankees' decision.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge desperately tried to return for the postseason after straining his calf, but the New York Yankees captain was wisely left off the Wild Card series roster.

Judge sustained a moderate soleus muscle strain in his calf and received a platelet-poor plasma (PPP) injection to try to speed up his rehab, but it wasn’t enough for him to make the roster for the team’s best-of-three series against the Boston Red Sox. Former college football quarterback-turned-foot-and-ankle surgeon Dr. Drew Burdi said if Judge came back too soon, he could leave himself exposed to further injury.

"If you do go too fast, too soon, you could just make it a more severe injury. It's a soleus, so that could lead to overstraining (the) hamstring, up and down. So that's your calf muscle, or part of the calf muscle. You could put more strain on your Achilles, you could put more strain on your hamstrings, and that could lead to other injuries," Burdi told OutKick in a recent interview.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Burdi explained that strains involve varying degrees of muscle tearing and that a premature return to play could cause Judge’s strain to go from moderate to severe. A more severe tear could lead to a much longer recovery time, regardless of the treatment used.

"If you're not ready to go back in yet, you tear it more, you can get to a point where the advanced conservative therapies like PRP injections, shock wave therapy, these guys are getting oxygen chamber therapy. This stuff can only go so far. The body can only adapt so much, can only heal so quickly," Burdi said.

The worst potential outcome of Judge returning too soon could be an Achilles rupture. Burdi said such an injury is a possibility.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Possibly, yeah, I mean, that's always a risk. Again, it, it kind of depends how he feels, but it's always a risk, and Achilles is always so scary because a lot of people, you see it in football, guys are jumping up on the sidelines and they come down weird and they rupture their Achilles. You're just like, wow, they don't even feel it before it happens," Burdi said.

"That's tough because those are tough injuries to come back from. Guys do do it, but they're never quite the same."

Burdi said that while Achilles injuries aren’t necessarily career killers, they are career changers.

So while the Yankees may have a Judgian-sized hole in their Wild Card Series lineup, leaving Judge off the roster could be the safer long-term approach. Judge said he intended to try to play in Game 1, but the three-time American League MVP didn’t recover in time.

While Judge might not have been hitting like himself in his seven games back from the rib injury that kept him out since June, going 4 for 23 with one home run and 13 strikeouts, his presence in the lineup was a boost. Even when the Yankees’ captain isn’t hitting, Judge’s presence in the lineup takes pressure off other hitters.

In 66 games this season, Judge is hitting .241 with 18 home runs and 41 RBI. He hopes the Yankees can eliminate the rival Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card Series so he can rejoin the team in the ALDS.
